reference_reviewed: The existing receipt parser plus its surrounding nonzero-return-code rejection; read as source without executing its controller.
interface: check_export_receipt(returncode, stdout_bytes, target_Path, html_raw_bytes, options_dict) returns the matching receipt dictionary or rejects by raising an exception; no exact exception class is prescribed.
valid_cases: plain log lines surrounding a complete JSON receipt line
mixed unrelated JSON records and one matching receipt line
one stale receipt and one matching receipt line
extra metadata on the matching receipt
empty input bytes with a nonempty output and exactly matching receipt
known_negative_cases: positive nonzero exit with a matching receipt
negative exit with a matching receipt
JSON array instead of the documented receipt object/JSON-line transport
missing expected artifact despite claimed success
empty artifact with otherwise matching receipt
duplicate matching receipts separated by log lines
invariants: Valid calls return the selected matching record, preserving metadata.
Calls do not alter input bytes, options or expected artifact bytes.
Probe fixtures are synthetic; no renderer, browser, model or external service is invoked.
The reference comparison preserves existing valid behavior; a synthetic exit-only checker is not substituted for the competent reference.
Matching receipts can be replayed for identical bytes/options; acceptance is not proof of fresh execution, PDF validity, readability or visual quality.
reporting: Report every case and valid/negative counts; retain raw details privately when requested. Sanitized results contain hashes, case identifiers and exception classes only, never source paths or private source contents. Known reference gaps are observations, not evidence of general speed/quality superiority.
